title: every-answered-question-rides-the-question-door
intention: Every question Akien has answered — today scattered across the 94 rulings, 48 ticket decision lines, and chat — stands as a resolved record in the question corpus, so the corpus is the one place the system reads its own Q&A and what really happens can be observed against it.
how: (1) one door verb question.migrate(ticket, question, answer, *, answered_at, source, raised_by) in cairn/tools/question/question.py — opens-and-resolves in one journaled act, date and answered_at from the SOURCE not the clock, source = the path it came from, refuses a duplicate (same ticket + source) so a re-run writes nothing; (2) a scratchpad-free migration script under cairn/tools/question/ (a task shipped as code so a bare box replays it) that reads decisions/*.json (the_ruling_verbatim + confirmation_verbatim → question + answer) and ticket decisions[] with by naming Akien (the quoted phrase → answer; the decision text → question, restated as a question ending '?'), and moves the 573 inline distinctions to distinctions[] and the 52 cast_check leftovers to cast_checks through the artifact door; (3) a census tooth over a fixture corpus + the live census on the verdict; (4) gated on 'once all this stuff is stable' — depends_on the question door PROVED (9adc6fddf185), the rehearsal machine PROVED (6b06fcb499fa), and the skills tier; runs last in tier 3.
falsifier: DONE when (1) every ruling under decisions/ with the_ruling_verbatim stands ALSO as a resolved open-* record bound to the ticket the ruling names (the first named when several, the rest in tickets_named; the ruling's own id when it names none), answer = his words verbatim (a list joined by newlines), date and answered_at = the ruling's date, source = decisions/<file> — decisions/ itself untouched; (2) every ticket decisions[] line whose by names Akien and quotes his words stands as a resolved open-* bound to that ticket, answer = the quoted phrases, and the line gains question: open-… beside by; a line citing a record already in the corpus is linked to it, not copied; a 'CC's call, per Akien' line (his standing delegation, CC answering) and a line with no words of his are counted out by name; (3) questions[] on every ticket holds open-* ids only — the D11 split (f00c49bd) moved them into the state file, not out: measured 2026-11-12, 625 inline {q, a} dicts stood in the state questions of 129 tickets (573 /sorted distinctions, 52 check bullets), none written since 2026-09-01 and none read; each ticket's whole standing list rides its log as a kind 'field' line, then the state keeps the open-* ids; (4) the migration is one door verb, question.migrate(...), journaled per record through the artifact door, idempotent (a second run writes 0 records); (5) the chat-log answers (his 'yes B', open-de25b82c3ced) stand too: a typed reply to a CC turn ending in '?' is copied, answer = his string verbatim, source = chat:<session>#<uuid>; counted out by name: secret-shaped replies, pairs about the CC0AC weather project (house details stay out of committed files), and command echoes; (6) the census before and after — python3 -m cairn.tools.question.migrate --census — reads outside = 0 for all four sources (rulings, decision lines, chat, inline) after, on the verdict by instrument. Proof: cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_every_answered_question_rides_the_door.py. RED if a migrated answer differs by one byte from its source, if decisions/ is written, or if a question is opened with a today-date instead of its source date. WRONG INTENT if his answer to the population question narrows it.
traces_to: Law 1 (every answered question becomes structure — an answer in a ruling packet or a chat log is one the corpus cannot count); Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now — one corpus, not three); memory rulings-are-questions-in-the-inbox. Telos: the system observes what really happens against the record of what was decided.

decisions.text: Census first, and it corrected the premise: the inline questions[] dicts are 573 distinctions + 52 cast_check leftovers, 0 questions. Akien's answers outside the corpus are the 94 rulings and the 48 by-Akien decision lines (chat answers unrecorded — his call, open-de25b82c3ced).

decisions.text: The widened population (open-de25b82c3ced 'yes B') measured 2026-11-12 by migrate --census: rulings 87; decision lines 144 naming Akien = 35 quoting his words + 9 citing a held record + 81 'CC's call, per Akien' + 19 with no words of his; chat 106 pairs after counting out 2 secret-shaped, 48 other-project, 6 command echoes.

A ruling's question is its own 'question' field when it ends in '?', else 'What is the ruling on: <title or slug>?'; a decision line's is its text restated '<text> — is that the decision?'; a chat pair's is the last sentence of CC's text ending in '?'. The question side is a translation; the answer side is never one.
